idiom_name: dynamic_cast cross cast from the degenerate Visitor base to a per-element visitor interface
implementation_notes: This is the pattern's home: a degenerate Visitor base with a pure virtual destructor, one abstract visitor per element declaring a single visit overload, concrete visitors that multiply-inherit only the element-visitor interfaces they implement, and an accept that performs the cross cast - if (auto* cv = dynamic_cast<CircleVisitor*>(&v)) cv->visit(*this); - with the failed cast meaning this visitor cannot visit this element. What the idiom replaces is the cyclic header dependency: an element includes only its own visitor interface, forward-declares the degenerate base, and never sees the other elements. Keep the classic Visitor when the element set is stable, because there the single visitor base with one overload per element turns a missing case into a compile error and removes the cast entirely.
pitfalls: Visitor must be a polymorphic class (typically a pure virtual destructor): dynamic_cast to or from a non-polymorphic base does not compile, and deleting a concrete visitor through a non-virtual destructor is undefined behaviour.
dynamic_cast cost depends on the size and shape of the hierarchy, and Martin explicitly warns that this makes the pattern a poor fit for hard real-time code with predictable latency budgets.
The failed cast needs a deliberate branch; silently ignoring it is the default the C++ listings call AcceptError, and it is the difference between a diagnosable no-op and dropped visits.
